purpose: Define the exact documented PBR baseline structure to compare against.
required_inputs: source artifacts; matrix construction rule; pair policy; diagonal policy; lag policy; metric definitions; hash lineage
excluded_inputs: new candidate fields; repaired fields; physical proxy fields
construction_or_randomization_rule: No execution here; future run must reconstruct only from documented artifacts.
target_metrics: rank; PSD_status; eigenvalue_spectrum; nullspace_dimension; lag_class_structure; block_or_toeplitz_like_pattern
success_condition: baseline source lineage and metric definitions are exact
failure_condition: missing lineage or ambiguous construction rule
allowed_interpretation: Baseline can be used as reference in future execution.
stop_rule: Stop if source artifact or matrix rule cannot be uniquely identified.

purpose: Test whether true lag-class membership plus matrix construction suffices.
required_inputs: pair identifiers; true lag-class membership; pair counts per lag class; documented matrix construction rule or projection-compatible substitute
excluded_inputs: all non-lag candidate variables; repaired candidate fields; physical proxy fields; speculative source fields
preserved_constraints: true lag memberships and documented pair constraints
construction_or_randomization_rule: Build minimal model using only lag-class membership and documented construction.
target_metrics: rank; PSD_status; eigenvalue_spectrum_similarity; nullspace_dimension; lag_class_coherence; class_cardinality_sensitivity
success_condition: target metrics match calibrated baseline better than controls
failure_condition: target metrics fail to match baseline
allowed_interpretation: Lag-class membership may be mathematically sufficient if controls fail.
stop_rule: Stop if true lag membership table is unavailable or ambiguous.

purpose: Test whether same cardinalities without true lag labels reproduce structure.
required_inputs: total pair count; number_of_classes; class_cardinalities; pair symmetry constraints; diagonal policy
excluded_inputs: true lag labels; candidate variables; physical proxy fields
preserved_constraints: same class count and cardinality distribution as true lag classes
construction_or_randomization_rule: Random or deterministic partitions unrelated to true lag classes with equal cardinalities.
success_condition: non-lag partitions fail to reproduce lag-specific structure
allowed_interpretation: Failure supports lag-specific sufficiency design; success supports generic partition artifact.
forbidden_interpretation: Non-lag failure proves physical lag causality.
stop_rule: Stop if equal-cardinality partitions cannot respect pair constraints.

purpose: Test class-count artifact independent of cardinality distribution.
required_inputs: total pair count; number_of_classes; valid random cardinalities
excluded_inputs: true lag labels; preserved true cardinalities
construction_or_randomization_rule: Randomize cardinalities within valid pair constraints.
success_condition: different-cardinality partitions fail where true lag model succeeds
failure_condition: same class count alone reproduces structure
allowed_interpretation: Structure may depend on cardinalities or lag geometry rather than class count alone.
stop_rule: Stop if valid randomized cardinalities cannot be generated without bias.

purpose: Check expected invariance under relabeling class names while preserving memberships.
required_inputs: true memberships; class labels; documented construction
failure_condition: metrics change under pure relabeling without documented reason
stop_rule: Stop if construction intentionally uses numeric lag labels as values; document this separately.

purpose: Destroy true memberships while preserving selected marginals.
required_inputs: pair identifiers; selected marginals; total count; class count
excluded_inputs: true lag memberships after destruction; candidate variables
construction_or_randomization_rule: Shuffle memberships while preserving marginals specified in protocol.
success_condition: structure collapses when memberships are destroyed
allowed_interpretation: Collapse supports nontrivial membership structure; survival suggests marginal artifact.
stop_rule: Stop if marginals are not explicitly defined before execution.

purpose: Check whether the construction rule alone guarantees target structure.
required_inputs: documented matrix rule; degenerate partitions; synthetic partitions; random partitions
excluded_inputs: true lag information; source data beyond required shape
construction_or_randomization_rule: Apply rule to degenerate, synthetic, and random partitions in future execution.
success_condition: rule-only controls do not reproduce target structure
allowed_interpretation: Structure may be construction theorem or tautology.
stop_rule: Stop if construction rule cannot be isolated from data content.

purpose: Assess whether PBR matrix can be represented or approximated as sum_l w_l P_l.
required_inputs: lag class memberships; candidate P_l definitions; documented matrix construction
excluded_inputs: altered construction rule; physical area assumptions
construction_or_randomization_rule: Define P_l as class-incidence/projector-like operators; check idempotence-like behavior, orthogonality, sum over classes, rank contribution, Gram/PSD implications.
allowed_interpretation: Projector/operator formalization is viable as mathematical description.
forbidden_interpretation: K is a physical area operator.
stop_rule: Stop if P_l definitions are not mathematically explicit.

purpose: Design handoff for testing sensitivity to construction order.
required_inputs: documented pipeline; pair policy; lag policy; kernel rule; spectral readout rule
preserved_constraints: same documented inputs across order variants
construction_or_randomization_rule: Future handoff variants: pair->lag->kernel->spectrum; lag->pair->kernel->spectrum; pair->kernel->lag-readout->spectrum.
failure_condition: no order sensitivity where expected or ambiguous pipeline
allowed_interpretation: Structure-birth audit is needed if order sensitivity appears.
stop_rule: Handoff only; stop before execution in this run.
